title.justification: The paper explores compositional generalization in dependency parsing by introducing a new dataset and analyzing a state-of-the-art parser.
title.quote: In this work, we introduce a gold-standard set of dependency parses for CFQ, and use this to analyze the behavior of a state-of-the-art dependency parser (Qi et al., 2020) on the CFQ dataset.

extractions.description: The paper proposes a benchmark for compositional generalization in dependency parsing, using a modified CFQ dataset with added dependency annotations. The authors analyze a dependency parser's performance using this dataset and explore the syntactic constructions that challenge the parser, discussing the disparities in performance across different data splits with various levels of compound divergence.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on computational linguistics and dependency parsing, rather than on climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Compositionality—the ability to combine familiar units like words into novel phrases and sentences—has been the focus of intense interest in artificial intelligence in recent years.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address any aspects of Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development. It is focused on improving models for understanding syntax and semantics in natural language processing.
